18/11/2026: London-headquartered finance software company Payhawk has raised £212.13 million in an all-equity Series C round led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, valuing the business at about £1.52 billion. All of its existing investors took part, including QED, Greenoaks, Lightspeed, Hedosophia and Bek Ventures, alongside new investors Galdana Ventures, Cogito Capital, Inveready and Invus, and the European entrepreneurs Tomas Okmanas and Didac Lee. The round takes Payhawk’s total funding to more than about £390 million and is subject to standard regulatory approvals. We covered Payhawk’s£14.3 million Series A led by QEDand its£83.7 million Series B led by Greenoaksin 2021.

Founded in Sofia, Payhawk is an AI-native spend management platform that brings bills, cards, expenses, travel and procurement together, with AI agents enforcing each company’s rules, policies and budgets on every payment. It serves mid-market and enterprise companies across 33 countries from 12 offices, and charges subscriptions rather than relying on card fees. The company says it was cash-flow positive in the third quarter of 2026 and still holds 70% of the money it raised in 2022. It will use the new funding to build what it calls a “Finance Operating System” for the AI era, combining AI agents, payments infrastructure and enterprise controls.

said Hristo Borisov, co-founder and CEO of Payhawk.

PAYHAWK LIMITED (11747263) was incorporated in England and Wales on 2 January 2019. Its registered office is on Chancery Lane in London, and its SIC code is 62090 (other information technology service activities). The co-founders on the register are Hristo Borisov (chief executive), Boyko Karadzhov and Konstantin Dzhengozov. The directors are Mehmed Selcuk Atici, Hristo Borisov, Boyko Karadzhov, William Kohler, Yusuf Ozdalga and Daniel Tomov. The company has filed a statement that it has no registrable person with significant control, as no one holds more than 25%. There are no charges on the register. Payhawk Limited is the UK top company of a group that was founded in Sofia and now operates across 33 countries from 12 offices. The group accounts are filed in the UK, and the equity goes into the UK company.

The share history is a classic venture ladder: Series Pre-Seed, Seed, A, B and B-1 Preferred shares, each with a starting price set in the articles. At today’s rates, the Series Seed price was about £1.12, the Series A about £5.46, the Series B about £33.07 and the Series B-1 about £54.86. The last allotment, of Series B-1 shares, was on 7 March 2022. On our calculation, the B-1 price valued the company at about £683 million at the time. In March 2023 Payhawk bought back and cancelled some shares (forms SH03 and SH06), and in September 2023 it adopted the currentarticles of association. The confirmation statement made on 1 January 2024 lists 12,216,216 shares. The statements made on 1 January 2025 and 1 January 2026 report no changes, and there has been no share allotment return (SH01) since the B-1 round.

The group accounts for 2025, filed on 5 October 2026, report net revenue of about £32.6 million, up 66%. The loss widened to about £28.0 million, from about £21.2 million in 2024. Cash at the year end was about £97.9 million, and the average headcount was 424. The release says the company was cash-flow positive in the third quarter of 2026 and still held about 70% of the money raised in 2022. Those are company statements we can’t check yet.

The Series C itself is not on the register yet. On 18 November 2026 Payhawk announced an all-equity round of about £212.13 million at a valuation of about £1,515 million, led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives. Every existing investor took part, including QED, Greenoaks, Lightspeed, Hedosophia and Bek Ventures, alongside new investors Galdana Ventures, Cogito Capital, Inveready and Invus, and the entrepreneurs Tomas Okmanas and Didac Lee. The release says total funding is now more than about £390 million and that completion is subject to standard regulatory approvals, which fits a payments group. When we checked Companies House on 23 November 2026 there was no new SH01, no new articles and no appointment of a Goldman Sachs director. “All-equity” means there is no debt in the round. The release doesn’t say whether the £1,515 million is the pre-money or post-money valuation, or whether any of the £212.13 million buys shares from existing holders (asecondary sale), so the shareholding below is the position before the round, followed by illustrations.

This is the shareholder list in the confirmation statement made on 1 January 2024, which the 2025 and 2026 statements confirm is unchanged. The percentages are our own calculation. Options are not on the register and are not included.

On this basis, the three co-founders hold 22.41% between them. The two HS Investments entities together hold 15.05%. Figures may not sum exactly because of rounding.

The Series C price is not public yet, so the table below is an illustration only. It works from the 12,216,216 shares on the register and ignores options and any anti-dilution shares, either of which would lower the founders’ figures.

Each scenario is an up round of about two times the 2022 price, so the anti-dilution protection in the articles should not be triggered.

The current articles were adopted by written resolution and filed on 5 October 2023. They refer to a subscription and shareholders’ agreement, which is not public. A Series C usually brings new articles, and we’ll update this section when they are filed.

Liquidation preference: all thepreference shares(Pre-Seed, Seed, A, B and B-1) rank together, 1x, ahead of the ordinary shares. The Preference Amount is unusual: it is the greater of the amount paid to the company and the price a holder paid when buying the share on a secondary sale. So an investor who bought preferred shares from another holder at a higher price gets that higher price back first.

Anti-dilution protection(article 7): the Series Seed, A, B and B-1 shares have weighted average protection (full ratchet and weighted average) if new shares are issued below their starting price.

Investor consent: an Investor Majority means holders of more than 50% of the B and B-1 shares held by the Participating Investors, and must include Digital East Fund and either Lightspeed or Greenoaks. Some matters need a Series B Majority, 75% of the Series B shares.

Board (board seat and observer, articles 12.2 to 12.5): several investors can appoint Investor Directors, including a Series B-1 Director. The release says James Hayward, Managing Director within Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, is joining the board, but no appointment had been filed when we checked.

Pre-emption rights: Participating Investors have a right of first refusal on shares that other holders want to sell (article 4.4).

Listing: a Qualifying IPO needs a price of at least three times the Series B-1 starting price, about £164.58 a share, and gross proceeds of at least about £41.9 million. On the register’s share count, that price implies a value of about £2.0 billion before new shares.

The three co-founders hold 22.41% together. In our scenarios they would hold between about 19.3% and 20.8% after the Series C, depending on whether the £1,515 million is pre-money or post-money and how much of the round is secondary. Hristo Borisov and Boyko Karadzhov would each hold about 9.5% to 10.3%. Seedilutionin our glossary. Try it yourself: model the round with thecap table and dilution simulator.

The announced valuation is about £1,515 million. If that is post-money, the pre-money valuation is about £1,303 million. If it is pre-money, the post-money valuation is about £1,727 million. Either way it is about 2.2 to 2.5 times the roughly £683 million post-money valuation of the 2022 B-1 round, and well intounicornterritory. The SH01 will settle the figure. Seevaluation,growth equityandseries B and later. Try it yourself: thevaluation and exit estimator.

This is an illustration, not a forecast. From about 19.3%, a pre-IPO round selling 10% would take the co-founders to about 17.4%, and an IPO issuing another 10% to about 15.6%. With revenue of about £32.6 million in 2025 and a valuation of about £1,515 million, the company is priced at about 46 times 2025 revenue, so growth has to continue for the next round to be an up round. Try it yourself: thecap table and dilution simulatorand therunway calculator.

This is also an illustration. Growth investors buying in at about £1,515 million would typically hope for three times their money, which points to a sale or listing at about £4.5 billion. Until the Series C terms are filed, we know only that the existing preferred shares rank together at 1x. The existing preference equals what each investor paid (or a higher secondary price), which is small next to a £1.5 billion valuation, so at that level the preference makes little difference to the founders. At about £4.5 billion, 19.3% would be worth about £870 million to the co-founders together, before tax and costs. Try it yourself: theliquidation preference calculatorand theVC method valuation.

We’d expect Goldman Sachs Alternatives to receive a new senior or pari passu Series C class, a board seat and consent rights. We’ll update this when the articles are filed. Try it yourself: ourterm sheets explainedguide and thefunding readiness check.
